name: Tryout
why: Borrowing any shop member's On Recruit is a clean idea with real aim, though it plays more like a copy than a recruit.

name: Gather
why: Plain fuel plus a recruit bonus; the same text sits on Stash and Allowance, so nobody at the table notices it.

name: Walk-In
why: A blind recruit from the pile (allowed randomness) with a small gift to rivals; whether you pay for it is not stated.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into a rival's better member is a big, aimable swing that hits the leader, though the two-step text needs a read.

name: Demote
why: Same swap as Promote but downward; useful for red count and Deprogrammers, less of a moment.

name: Initiation
why: A free member up to 8 is a strong, readable round III finisher; the choice is mostly just the best card.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Every round a same-cost swap with a rival: aimable, fair to the victim, countered by Loyalists.

name: Volunteer
why: Vanilla 1-for-1 body; only matters as red count or swap fodder.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two members for one recruit is a real red burst and feeds Proselytizers and Recruiter.

name: Proselytizers
why: A quiet per-recruit trickle that only pays the player already recruiting most; no one reacts.

name: Mob
why: Big round-end payout for leading red count; rivals can race red members, but it pays the leader.

name: Recruiter
why: 5 red for +1 red per recruit is a forgettable trickle that rarely pays back.

name: Patriarch
why: Generic game-end per-member scorer that would sit the same in any color.

name: Greeters
why: Cheap 2-count that adds color to every On Recruit across colors; invisible to rivals.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Worth 4 for 3 is a must-buy regardless of its ability; the sting on swaps is a nice red link.

name: Panel
why: A Promote or Demote stapled to a recruit chains red swaps; strong and aimable.

name: Loyalists
why: Red's own answer to swaps; clear block that rivals feel when Body Snatchers or Promote whiff.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round for 5 resources: dull, ties to nothing in the color, never worth buying.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for giving up tempo, and the Goes Last token links the contest, Last Call and Night Watch.

name: Hold Up
why: A skip you can aim by timing, even at yourself; feeds Gossip and meets Early Birds.

name: Right Away
why: Double turn for tempo with small purple; clean and timing-driven.

name: Last Call
why: Pays more the more minions you hold back, a real gamble on spaces staying open; token rules need a read.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row is a rule bend you feel; you pick the moment to grab key spaces.

name: Overtime
why: +1 minion in round III is plain and strong.

name: Courier
why: Turns double turns into a color spread; combos with Right Away, Crunch Time and snake ends.

name: Night Watch
why: Passive payout on rivals taking the token; unclear whose minions count and no choice for the owner.

name: Night Owls
why: A permanent extra minion from round II is a strong, readable purple rule bend.

name: Early Birds
why: Cheap 2-count with a narrow block against skips; matters only if Hold Up or Bouncers show.

name: Bouncers
why: A double skip on recruit is a felt table moment with timing choice; meets Gossip and Early Birds.

name: Gossip
why: Pays on every skip at the table, nice link to Hold Up and Bouncers, but rivals never feel it.

name: Timekeeper
why: Same per-own-color game-end shape as Snobs, Old Money and Chronicler; rewards the leader.

name: Closer
why: Ties straight into the went-last contest and token play; a race rivals can see.

name: Hot Streak
why: A one-shot payoff for chaining turns builds toward a moment, though counting turns just before needs care.

name: Shift Crew
why: Worth 4 for 4 with no ability: must-buy filler that has nothing to do with turns.

name: Night Shift
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do: which minion was placed before which skip, and who held the token when
why: A chain of conditions nobody can read cold or track on a table.

name: Toast
why: Big scaling silver with a gift to every rival that feeds their contest; simple and on theme.

name: Polish
why: A clean conversion that nobody else notices; overlaps Sweet Talk and Polisher.

name: Party Gifts
why: Aimed gifts that buy followers but feed rivals' silver contest: the color's core tension in one line.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pay you a resource and get silver back; mild trade, rivals choose the cheapest.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus free conversion; useful but solitary and repeats Polish.

name: Largesse
why: Up to 10 silver to rivals in round III right before a 10-follower silver contest: a real who-do-I-crown choice.

name: Godparent
why: Cash out a member as a gift; combos with Old Maid, Martyrs and rival dumping.

name: Hostesses
why: Steady gift engine that feeds rivals' contest automatically; no aim.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver on gifts, unclear per gift or per silver; forgettable.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 follower for taking your own color's spaces; generic trickle.

name: Debutantes
why: Double your silver once is a big, timed contest swing; the gift to rivals is a nice tax.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as any color is a strong rule bend but overlaps Polish, Sweet Talk and Alchemists at 11 cost.

name: Philanthropist
why: A smaller Largesse on a card; fine gift play but repeats the spaces.

name: Polisher
why: A one-shot Polish on a card; repeats a sibling.

name: Creditor
why: Take 2 followers from the leader and pay them silver: aimable catch-up that feeds the gift tension.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Collecting back the silver you gifted, timed before the contest, closes the color's loop.

name: High Society
why: Taxes rivals using silver spaces; a passive deterrent with no choice for the owner.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources than you
why: Pays only when a rival holds more silver than you; the leader's hoard funds you.

name: Harvest
why: Yellow's plain fuel space: any colors, which feeds full sets; the anchor.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the wheel to pick a color; small but aimed at where rivals sit.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a first member of a new color; good aim but nobody else feels it.

name: Big New Blood
why: A bigger New Blood one ring up; repeats the round I space.

name: Melting Pot
why: Pays for a broad cult; clean, but solitary.

name: Makeover
why: Rearranging your whole pile in round III snipes any contest; a visible swing rivals must read.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills empty colors each round, helping sets and the player who lacks; nobody else notices.

name: Customs Officer
why: +1 yellow when robbed or changed; tiny, reactive, never a reason to buy.

name: Tourist
why: A steady per-color follower income; strong but solitary.

name: Harmonist
why: Game-end full sets scorer; on theme but quiet and leader-friendly.

name: Dyer
why: Same per-color shape as Tourist and Caravan but paying yellow; autopilot.

name: Meddler
why: Changing a resource of each rival can break a set or a contest lead; small but aimed.

name: Drifters
why: A chosen-color member plays off New Blood, Big Tent and member-count contests; needs a marker for the color.

name: Big Tent
why: Rewards one of each color, which red swaps can break; a clear long plan.

name: Caravan
why: Strong per-color income but a third copy of the Dyer/Tourist shape.

name: Tastemaker
why: Only Meddler changes rivals' resources in yellow, so this is nearly dead.

name: Savings
why: Blue plus a bury to deny a rival's target; quiet but real.

name: Out of Style
why: Wiping a whole color from the shop is a felt, aimed denial that pays you per card.

name: Peek
why: Pile control and good blue; the reorder sets up later shops, but text has two parts to read.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two buys in one turn is the clean blue rule bend.

name: Bury
why: Denial plus blue; the half-cost math adds a step.

name: Spree
why: Three buys in round III; a big finish for a stocked player.

name: Hawker
why: Rivals each decide to pay you a premium or let you have it free: a real table moment with both sides weighed.

name: Patroness
why: Pays on every bury at the table, tying into blue's spaces; unclear per member or per event; rivals don't feel it.

name: Snobs
why: Per-own-color game-end scorer; same shape as three others.

name: Window Shopper
why: Burying two shop cards each round for their colors: denial with aim.

name: Shopaholics
why: Permanent double buys is a big engine that runs away for the richest player.

name: Window Dressers
why: A one-time shop wipe on a cheap 3-count; the count is the reason to buy.

name: Doormen
why: A forced trade of a rival's member through the shop; strong but reads like red and needs care.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue when you buy followers; nothing to do with the shop.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit churns the shop; feeds Patroness and Scavenger.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when rivals buy blue; small, passive.

name: Scavenger
why: Turns every rival bury into your chance to grab the card; a counter to blue's own denial.

name: Help Yourself
why: A big split steal you aim at the leader's pile; the color's core.

name: Stash
why: The same text as Gather and Allowance; nothing magenta about it.

name: Lie Low
why: A small steal plus a round of safety; a block rivals see.

name: Heist
why: Three followers straight off a rival; aimable catch-up.

name: Shake Down
why: The victim picks their own punishment, which feels bad to be hit by.

name: Poach
why: Take any rival member free in round III: a big aimed swing, late enough to be fair.

name: Cutpurse
why: Cheap steady drain on the richest rival; good check on hoards, autopilot.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap one-shot steal of 3; clear and fine.

name: Grifter
why: Steal scales with your member count, so it pays the big cult; 8 cost.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A steal timed right before contests swings any rim; rivals see it coming.

name: Desperado
why: Steals grow while you trail: a clear catch-up card.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse; repeats a sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: The color's shield; also protects a leader's hoard.

name: Double Agent
why: Trade itself for a rival's better member; aimable, reads a bit red.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member from the biggest cult every round; the victim loses members early with no answer.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal on every recruit; steady and on theme.

name: Fence
why: Thieves pay you; a deterrent rivals feel.

name: Allowance
why: Same text as Gather and Stash; the white tie is only the followers.

name: Splurge
why: Turns a big buy into followers; round III rate unstated.

name: Exchange
why: A clean 2-for-1 follower trade that nobody else notices.

name: Farewell
why: Cash a member for its cost in followers; plays off Martyrs and the shop.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell paid in white instead; repeats its sibling.

name: Cash In
why: All white to followers in round III; a satisfying finish, solitary.

name: Recluse
why: Pays for a small cult against bigger rivals; fits fewest followers and fights Blue's contest.

name: Landlord
why: Steady +2 white; works the same in any cult.

name: Heiresses
why: 9 cost for a one-time per-member white pile; weak and leader-friendly.

name: Brokers
why: A bonus on white follower spaces; unclear on copies, quiet.

name: Misers
why: Holding white for game end fights Cash In and invites theft; a real hold choice.

name: Raiders
why: A one-shot follower steal that pays the victim; reads magenta.

name: Cashier
why: A Cash In on a card; timing choice, but repeats the space.

name: Money Changers
why: Paid by every follower buy at the table; cheap 2-count, passive.

name: Martyrs
why: Taking it from you pays you; deters thieves and swaps and combos with Farewell.

name: Old Money
why: Per-own-color game-end scorer; same shape as three others.

name: Hoarder
why: Sets up a Cash In or Misers payoff; solitary.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain fuel space; the anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action: plays off whatever the last player did.

name: Reprise
why: Doubles your own best space; solitary.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; aimable at their best card.

name: Cover
why: Copy an empty space; flexible, solitary.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Replay every On Recruit you own; a payoff for a whole game of buying.

name: Busker
why: Steady +2 green; works the same in any cult.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrowing a rival's best ability each round is strong; needs a marker for who it copies.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 per copy at the table; tiny trickle.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubling copied gains is a strong green engine, invisible to rivals.

name: Fan Club
why: Copies a space the leader holds: aims at the front-runner.

name: Roadie
why: Per-green-member income; rewards the big green cult.

name: Stunt Double
why: Doubles the space you just took, any color; a timing choice.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do every action a rival took this round: a huge moment, but the order and timing need a ruling at 14 cost.

name: Doppelganger
why: Copy your best member; doubles the leader's engine.

name: Agents
why: A block on being copied; matters only against Green.

name: Chronicler
why: Per-own-color game-end scorer; same shape as three others.

name: Party Crasher
why: Joining a taken space breaks blocking once; aimable catch-up.

name: Alchemists
why: Cheap 3-count that makes every cost easy; nobody notices.

name: Extra Hand
why: 9 cost for one extra minion once; rarely worth it.

name: Line Cutters
why: 2 cost for 3 followers and first every round: a must-buy that kills the catch-up turn order.

name: Old Maid
why: A poison card to dump on rivals with Godparent, Promote or Double Agent; a table laugh.

name: Dabblers
why: Wild for color counts; unclear which counts and what it is at any moment.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members anywhere each round; strong aimable chaos tool.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel a contest you can't win; a clear spite card the leader can see coming.

name: Con Men
why: A bigger Accomplice with no color cost; makes magenta's card look weak.

name: Sore Loser
why: Takes followers from the top contest winner if you win none; catch-up, tie case unstated.
